results.title: The Benefits of Dance Therapy in Rehabilitation - Knowledge Voyager
results.content: # The Benefits of Dance Therapy in Rehabilitation. This innovative form of therapy, also known as Dance/Movement Therapy (DMT), uses movement and dance as a means of communication and expression, aiming to improve the physical, emotional, and mental well-being of individuals. It is based on the premise that the body and mind are interconnected and that changes in the body can affect the mind and vice versa. The American Dance Therapy Association (ADTA) defines Dance Therapy as “the psychotherapeutic use of movement to promote emotional, social, cognitive, and physical integration of the individual, for the purpose of improving health and well-being.”. It has been found to be beneficial for people of all ages and with various health conditions, including those recovering from physical injuries, suffering from mental health disorders, or dealing with chronic illnesses. The American Dance Therapy Association defines dance/movement therapy as the psychotherapeutic use of movement to promote emotional, social, cognitive, and physical integration of the individual, for the purpose of improving health and well-being.

results.title: Therapeutic Dance vs. Dance Therapy: 5 important differences
results.content: Dance Therapy: 5 important differences. Both therapeutic dance and dance therapy are beneficial, needed and, in many cases, necessary. Therapeutic dance, often taught by an artist, teacher or therapist is more commonly referred to as instruction, whereas dance therapy, led by a master’s level certified dance therapist, typically involves facilitation. More often than not, therapeutic dance is teaching movement or dance steps, while dance therapy is using movement to process emotional or behavioral health. While therapeutic dance focuses on movement goals, dance therapy typically focuses on psychosocial goals or behavioral intervention. Dance therapy, on the other hand, is a form of psychotherapy that relies on the relationship between client and therapist. In dance therapy, the focus is on the process or, more specifically, verbally processing, when possible, and finding symbolism through movement as it emerges in each session. Therapeutic dance will more commonly result in a performance or demonstration of achievement, whereas dance therapy may continue until a client is no longer appropriate or reasons for entering therapy have been resolved. Dance therapy, which may include certain dance forms, is guided by the therapist’s theoretical framework such as Cognitive-Behavioral, Person-Centered or Psychoanalytic theories. While both therapeutic dance and dance therapy can have components confidential in nature, confidentiality is not a required aspect of therapeutic dance. As a dance instructor, studio owner or artistic director, if you notice that a student or company member is dealing with a mental health issue that is impacting his/her ability to learn, perform or even enjoy dance, you may want to refer the individual to a dance/movement therapist. Please note that there is a lot of overlap between therapeutic dance and dance therapy. Dance therapy, although commonly used to describe therapeutic dance, is actually a profession and quite different from dance used as therapy. *For more information on dance/movement therapy, check out the American Dance Therapy Association.*. By Erica Hornthal, LCPC, BC-DMT, Dance/Movement Therapist, Chicago Dance Therapy.
